source: Methanol Magic LLC, "Methanol Plant Feasibility Study", ChE473k, University of Texas at Austin, Spring 2015 -- Supplementary Table A12 (storage tanks TK-3501/2/3) and Table 4 (Chilton method factors). Student design report, not peer reviewed.
further_description: Installed cost per MWh of CRUDE methanol (64.5 wt% MeOH, 35 wt% water) in USABLE volume. Table A12 per tank: 80609 cuft = 2282.6 m3, bare 825100 USD = 361.5 USD/m3. x4.952 Chilton fixed-capital factor (Table 4: 1.43 x (1+0.40+0.07+0.15+0.50+0.10) x (1+0.35+0.20+0.01)) = 1790 USD/m3 installed; /0.83 fluid volume = 2157 USD/m3 usable; /3.045 MWh_MeOH per m3 of crude (methanol 791.0 kg/m3, water 998.2 kg/m3, LHV 19.9 GJ/t, ideal mixing) = 708 USD/MWh; x0.9009 ECB USD-EUR mid-2015 = 637.8 EUR/MWh in 2015 EUR. Interpretation of Table A12 cross-checks: tank geometry pi/4 x 61ft^2 x 28ft = 2317 m3 confirms the capacity is per tank (1.5%); and 3 tanks x 2282.6 x 0.83 = 5684 m3 against 3 holding days of the plant output 165811670 gal/yr over 330 day/yr = 5706 m3 confirms both the 83% fill and that the 3 holding days are the total across all three tanks (99.6%). UPPER BOUND: the source tank is SS316-clad, dearer than a plain carbon-steel atmospheric tank. Design guidance (no costs) in Methanol Institute, Atmospheric Above Ground Tank Storage of Methanol: carbon steel with stainless cladding, and methanol is hygroscopic so the free-board needs dry-nitrogen padding.
